<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

% Determine number of rows in the input (N)
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.

% Determine maximum color M
max_color(M) :-
    color(M),
    #count{R : input(R, _, M)} > 0,
    not (color(D), D > M, #count{R : input(R, _, D)} > 0).

% Subcells of max color
max_cell(I,J) :- max_color(M), input(I, J, M).

% Compute block row index for a cell (R,C)
block_row(R,BR) :- BR = #min{BR : R >= N*BR, R < N*(BR+1)}.
block_col(C,BC) :- BC = #min{BC : C >= N*BC, C < N*(BC+1)}.
sub_i(R,BR,I) :- R = N*BR + I, I >= 0, I < N.
sub_j(C,BC,J) :- C = N*BC + J, J >= 0, J < N.

% Wall cells (max color cells in the output)
wall(R,C) :-
    max_cell(I,J),
    max_color(M),
    R = N*BR + I,
    C = N*BC + J,
    block_row(R,BR),
    block_col(C,BC),
    sub_i(R,BR,I),
    sub_j(C,BC,J).

% Candidate cells (non-wall)
candidate(R,C) :- not wall(R,C).

% Output grid size
size(Size) :- Size = N * N.

% BFS: cells reachable from the boundary via candidate cells
boundary_passable(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), R = 0.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), R = Size-1.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), C = 0.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), C = Size-1.

outside(R,C) :- boundary_passable(R,C).
outside(R2,C2) :- outside(R1,C1), neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1), candidate(R2,C2), R2 >= 0, C2 >= 0, R2 < Size, C2 < Size.

% Interior cells: candidate but not reachable
interior(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), not outside(R,C).

% Output cell existence (generated by tiling of input)
output_cell(R,C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _),
    input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR),
    n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR,
    C = BC*NC + DC.

% Output assignment (mutually exclusive)
output(R,C,Color) :-
    max_color(M),
    wall(R,C),
    Color = M.
output(R,C,Color) :-
    max_color(M),
    candidate(R,C),
    interior(R,C),
    Color = M.
output(R,C,Color) :-
    max_color(M),
    candidate(R,C),
    outside(R,C),
    Color = 0.

% Exactly one answer set
1 { output(R, C, Color) :-
    output_cell(R, C),
    output(R, C, Color)
 } 1 :- true.

% Dimensions
N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
outRows = N * N.
outCols = M * M.

% Max colour (the unique largest colour that actually appears)
maxcol(Mc) :-
    color(Mc),
    #count{R : input(R, _, Mc)} > 0,
    not (color(D), D > Mc, #count{R : input(R, _, D)} > 0).

% Relative position in the input and its colour
srcColor(R,C,V) :-
    Rdiv = R / N,
    srcR = R - N * Rdiv,
    Cdiv = C / M,
    srcC = C - M * Cdiv,
    input(srcR, srcC, V).

% Output cell must be inside the output grid
output_range(R,C) :-
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    R >= 0, R < outRows,
    C >= 0, C < outCols.

% Passable cells: non‑max cells
passable(R,C) :-
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V).

% Cells on the boundary of the output that are passable
boundary_passable(R,C) :- passable(R,C), R = 0.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- passable(R,C), R = outRows - 1.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- passable(R,C), C = 0.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- passable(R,C), C = outCols - 1.

% Reachable cells via 4‑connected passable neighbours
reachable(R,C) :- boundary_passable(R,C).
reachable(R2,C2) :-
    reachable(R1,C1),
    neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1),
    passable(R2,C2).

% 4‑connected neighbours
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1 + 1, C2 = C1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1 - 1, C2 = C1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1, C2 = C1 + 1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1, C2 = C1 - 1.

% Output colour
output(R,C,0) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V),
    reachable(R,C).

output(R,C,Clr) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    maxcol(Clr),
    V = Clr.

output(R,C,Clr) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V),
    not reachable(R,C),
    maxcol(Clr).

% Exactly one colour per output cell
#count{R,C,Clr : output(R,C,Clr)} = 1.

% Exactly one answer set
1 { output(R,C,Clr) : true } 1 :- true.

% Determine the number of rows and columns of the input
n_rows(Rc) :- Rc = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(Cc) :- Cc = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Determine the maximum colour in the input
max_color(M) :-
    color(M),
    #count{R : input(R, _, M)} > 0,
    not (color(D), D > M, #count{R : input(R, _, D)} > 0).

% Cells that have the maximum colour
max_cell(I,J) :- max_color(M), input(I, J, M).

% Mapping an output cell to a sub‑cell of the input
block_row(R,BR) :- R = Cc * BR + I, I >= 0, I < Rc.
block_col(C,BC) :- C = Rc * BC + J, J >= 0, J < Cc.

% Walls: copies of the max colour in the output
wall(R,C) :-
    max_color(M),
    max_cell(I,J),
    block_row(R,BR),
    block_col(C,BC).

% Non‑wall (candidate) cells
candidate(R,C) :- not wall(R,C).

% Output size (rows = Cc * Rc, cols = Cc * Cc)
% Boundary of the output grid
boundary_passable(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), R = 0.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), R = Cc * Rc - 1.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), C = 0.
boundary_passable(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), C = Cc * Cc - 1.

% Flood‑fill through candidate cells
outside(R,C) :- boundary_passable(R,C).
outside(R2,C2) :- outside(R1,C1), neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1), candidate(R2,C2), R2 >= 0, C2 >= 0, R2 < Cc * Rc, C2 < Cc * Cc.

% Interior candidate cells (enclosed by the max colour)
interior(R,C) :- candidate(R,C), not outside(R,C).

% Existence of an output cell (tiled from the input)
output_cell(R,C) :-
    input(BR,BC,_),
    input(DR,DC,_),
    n_rows(Rc),
    n_cols(Cc),
    R = BR * Rc + DR,
    C = BC * Cc + DC.

% Output colour (exactly one colour per cell)
output(R,C,Color) :-
    max_color(M),
    wall(R,C),
    Color = M.
output(R,C,Color) :-
    max_color(M),
    candidate(R,C),
    interior(R,C),
    Color = M.
output(R,C,Color) :-
    max_color(M),
    candidate(R,C),
    outside(R,C),
    Color = 0.

% Exactly one answer set
1 { output(R, C, Color) :-
    output_cell(R, C),
    output(R, C, Color)
 } 1 :- true.

% 4‑connected neighbours for the flood‑fill
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :- R2 = R1+1, C2 = C1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :- R2 = R1-1, C2 = C1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :- R2 = R1,   C2 = C1+1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :- R2 = R1,   C2 = C1-1.

% Determine dimensions of the input
n_rows(Nr) :- Nr = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(Mc) :- Mc = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output grid bounds
in_output(R,C) :- R >= 0, R < Nr*Nr, C >= 0, C < Mc*Mc.

% A cell is covered by a non‑zero source copy if it originates from a non‑zero cell at (srcR,srcC) and the source offset (srcR,srcC) and a relative cell (dr,dc) from the input.
covered(R,C) :-
    input(srcR,srcC,srcColor),
    srcColor != 0,
    input(dr,dc,_),
    R = srcR * Nr + dr,
    C = srcC * Mc + dc.

% Output colour for cells that are covered by a non‑zero copy.
output(R,C,Color) :-
    in_output(R,C),
    covered(R,C),
    input(srcR,srcC,srcColor), srcColor != 0,
    input(dr,dc,Color),
    R = srcR * Nr + dr,
    C = srcC * Mc + dc.

% Output colour for cells that are not covered (they become 0).
output(R,C,Color) :-
    in_output(R,C),
    -covered(R,C),
    Color = 0.

% Exactly one answer set – the solution must be unique.
1 { output(R, C, Color) :-
    output(R, C, Color)
 } 1 :- true.

% color(0..9) is injected automatically.

% Determine the dimensions of the input grid
n_rows(Nr) :- Nr = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(Mc) :- Mc = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output grid bounds (output is Nr*Nr rows and Mc*Mc cols)
in_output(R,C) :- R >= 0, R < Nr*Nr, C >= 0, C < Mc*Mc.

% A cell is covered by a non‑zero copy if the source cell (srcR,srcC) has a non‑zero value
covered(R,C) :-
    input(srcR,srcC,srcColor),
    srcColor != 0,
    input(dr,dc,_),
    R = srcR * Nr + dr,
    C = srcC * Mc + dc.

% Output colour for cells that are covered by a non‑zero copy
output(R,C,Color) :-
    in_output(R,C),
    covered(R,C),
    input(srcR,srcC,srcColor), srcColor != 0,
    input(dr,dc,Color),
    R = srcR * Nr + dr,
    C = srcC * Mc + dc.

% Output colour for cells that are not covered (they become 0)
output(R,C,Color) :-
    in_output(R,C),
    -covered(R,C),
    Color = 0.

% Exactly one answer set (unique solution)
1 { output(R, C, Color) :-
    output(R, C, Color)
 } 1 :- true.

% color(0..9) facts are provided automatically.

% dimensions
nrows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
ncols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

    color(C),
    #count{R : input(R, _, C)} > 0,
    not (color(D), D > C, #count{R : input(R, _, D)} > 0).

% max colour variable
maxcol(M) :- max_color(M).

% output dimensions
outRows = N * N.
outCols = M * M.

% base cell colour (before interior fill)
output_cell(R,C,B) :-
    maxcol(M0),                     % M0 is the max colour
    input(SR,SC,M0),
    input(DR,DC,T),
    R = SR * N + DR,
    C = SC * M + DC,
    B = T.
output_cell(R,C,B) :-
    input(SR,SC,V),
    not maxcol(V),
    input(DR,DC,T),
    R = SR * N + DR,
    C = SC * M + DC,
    B = 0.

% max wall cells (used for flood fill)
max_wall(R,C) :- input(R,C,M0).

% boundary cells of the output grid
boundary(R,C) :- R = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- R = outRows - 1.
boundary(R,C) :- C = 0.
boundary(R,C) :- C = outCols - 1.

% reachable cells via 4‑connected movement through non‑max cells
reachable(R,C) :-
    boundary(R,C),
    output_cell(R,C,B),
    not maxcol(B).

reachable(R2,C2) :-
    reachable(R1,C1),
    neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1),
    output_cell(R2,C2,B),
    not maxcol(B).

% interior cells (non‑max and not reachable)
interior(R,C) :-
    output_cell(R,C,B),
    not maxcol(B),
    not reachable(R,C).

% final colours
output(R,C,M0) :-
    output_cell(R,C,B),
    B = M0.

output(R,C,0) :-
    output_cell(R,C,B),
    not maxcol(B),
    reachable(R,C).

output(R,C,M0) :-
    output_cell(R,C,B),
    not maxcol(B),
    interior(R,C).

    true

% 4‑connected neighbours

% Dimensions
nRows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nCols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Max colour
max_color(C) :-
    color(C),
    #count{R : input(R, _, C)} > 0,
    not (color(D), D > C, #count{R : input(R, _, D)} > 0).

% Variables for max colour
maxR(Rmax) :- max_color(C), Rmax = #max{R : input(R, _, C)}.
maxC(Cmax) :- max_color(C), Cmax = #max{C : input(_, C, C)}.
minR(Rmin) :- max_color(C), Rmin = #min{R : input(R, _, C)}.
minC(Cmin) :- max_color(C), Cmin = #min{C : input(_, C, C)}.

% Corner cell is max coloured?
corner_max :- max_color(C), maxR(Rmax), maxC(Cmax), input(Rmax, Cmax, C).

% Zero blocks
zero_block(R,C) :-
    input(SR, SC, 0),
    input(DR, DC, _),
    R = SR * N + DR,
    C = SC * M + DC.

% Region A (top-left block) with conditional size
output(R,C,Color) :-
    not zero_block(R,C),
    R >= Rmin,
    C >= Cmin,
    Color = C,
    corner_max,
    R <= maxR + N,
    C <= maxC + M.

output(R,C,Color) :-
    not zero_block(R,C),
    R >= Rmin,
    C >= Cmin,
    Color = C,
    not corner_max,
    R <= maxR + N - 1,
    C <= maxC + M - 1.

% Region B (bottom-right block)
output(R,C,Color) :-
    not zero_block(R,C),
    R >= maxR + N,
    R <= maxR + 2*N,
    C >= maxC + M,
    C <= maxC + 2*M,
    Color = C.

% Cells not covered by any of the above become zero
output(R,C,Color) :-

M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
outRows = N * N.
outCols = M * M.

% Max colour (the unique largest colour)
maxcol(Mc) :-
    color(Mc),
    #count{R : input(R, _, Mc)} > 0,
    not (color(D), D > Mc, #count{R : input(R, _, D)} > 0).

% Helper predicate to get the value from the input at the relative position
srcColor(R,C,V) :-
    Rdiv = R / N,
    srcR = R - N * Rdiv,
    Cdiv = C / M,
    srcC = C - M * Cdiv,
    input(srcR, srcC, V).

% Output coordinates must be within the output grid
output_range(R,C) :-
    R >= 0, R < outRows,
    C >= 0, C < outCols,
    srcColor(R,C,V).

% Passable cells: non‑max cells
passable(R,C) :-
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V).

% Boundary cells of the output grid
boundary(R,C) :-
    R = 0.
boundary(R,C) :-
    R = outRows - 1.
boundary(R,C) :-
    C = 0.
boundary(R,C) :-
    C = outCols - 1.

% Passable cells that lie on the boundary
boundary_passable(R,C) :- passable(R,C), boundary(R,C).

% Reachable cells via 4‑connected passable neighbours
reachable(R,C) :- boundary_passable(R,C).
reachable(R2,C2) :-
    reachable(R1,C1),
    neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1),
    passable(R2,C2).

% 4‑connected neighbours
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1 + 1, C2 = C1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1 - 1, C2 = C1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1, C2 = C1 + 1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1, C2 = C1 - 1.

% Output colour
output(R,C,0) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V),
    reachable(R,C).

output(R,C,Clr) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    maxcol(Clr),
    V = Clr.

output(R,C,Clr) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V),
    not reachable(R,C),
    maxcol(Clr).

% Exactly one colour per output cell
#count{R,C,Clr : output(R,C,Clr)} = 1.

% Exactly one answer set
1 { output(R,C,Clr) : true } 1 :- true.

<asp>
% Dimensions
N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
outRows = N * N.
outCols = M * M.

% Max colour (the largest colour that appears)
maxcol(Mc) :-
    color(Mc),
    #count{R : input(R, _, Mc)} > 0,
    not (color(D), D > Mc, #count{R : input(R, _, D)} > 0).

% Relative position in the input and its colour
srcColor(R,C,V) :-
    Rdiv = R / N,
    srcR = R - N * Rdiv,
    Cdiv = C / M,
    srcC = C - M * Cdiv,
    input(srcR, srcC, V).

% Output cell must be inside the output grid
output_range(R,C) :-
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    R >= 0, R < outRows,
    C >= 0, C < outCols.

% Passable cells: non‑max cells
passable(R,C) :-
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V).

% Cells on the boundary of the output grid that are passable
boundary_passable(R,C) :-
    passable(R,C),
    (R = 0) or (R = outRows-1) or (C = 0) or (C = outCols-1).

% Reachable cells via 4‑connected passable neighbours
reachable(R,C) :-
    boundary_passable(R,C).
reachable(R2,C2) :-
    reachable(R1,C1),
    neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1),
    passable(R2,C2).

% 4‑connected neighbours
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1 + 1, C2 = C1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1 - 1, C2 = C1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1, C2 = C1 + 1.
neighbor(R2,C2,R1,C1) :-
    R2 = R1, C2 = C1 - 1.

% Output colour
output(R,C,0) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V),
    reachable(R,C).

output(R,C,Clr) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    maxcol(Clr),
    V = Clr.

output(R,C,Clr) :-
    output_range(R,C),
    srcColor(R,C,V),
    not maxcol(V),
    not reachable(R,C),
    maxcol(Clr).

% Exactly one colour per output cell
#count{R,C,Clr : output(R,C,Clr)} = 1.

% Exactly one answer set
1 { output(R,C,Clr) : true } 1 :- true.
</asp>
